title: A simple protocol for extraction, derivatization, and analysis of tomato leaf and fruit lipophilic metabolites using GC-MS
protocol: Harvest plant tissue (500mg-1.0g) from under desired experimental conditions.
Immediately freeze the harvested tissue by immersing in liquid nitrogen.
Store lyophilized tissue at -80°C for several weeks or process immediately.
Transfer 300-500mg of lyophilized tissue to a glass vial with cap.
Add 10µl of internal standard 5α-cholest 7en-3β-ol (1mg/ml stock) to the vial.
Add 3.75ml of CHCl3: methanol (1:2) and vortex vigorously.
Add 1.25 ml of CHCl3 and vortex well.
Add 1.25 ml of dH2O and vortex once again.
Transfer bottom organic phase to a fresh vial with the help of a pipette.
Allow solvent to evaporate completely at 35°C.
Add 500 µl of 6% methanolic KOH (w/v) to the dried residue and incubate at 85°C for ½ -1 hours.
To it, add half the volume i.e., 250 µl of dH2O and then equal volume i.e., 750 µl of n-heptane and vortex well.
Allow layers to separate. Transfer upper phase to a fresh vial.
Repeat the above step twice using remaining volumes.
Allow heptane to evaporate completely (16-24 hours).
Add 100 µl of derivatization reagent (80 µl BFSTA + 20 µl TMCS) to the dried residue.
Incubate at 65°C for 1 hour.
Inject the sample into GC-MS in split mode.
Use a Rtx5MS column with dimensions 30m, 0.25-mm ID, and 0.25µm df.
Set the injection temperature to 300°C.
Set the interface temperature to 300°C.
Adjust the ion source to 250°C.
Use helium as carrier gas at a flow rate of 1 ml/min.
Perform analysis with an initial isothermal heating period at 100°C for 1 minute, followed by heating to 300°C for 20 minutes.
Record mass spectra at 2 scans per second over the range of 40 to 850 m/z.
Quantify each component based on peak areas and normalization using an internal standard.
